newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Nova Scotia to buy 70 pct of Banco Quilmes.
newsitem.headline: Nova Scotia to buy 70 pct of Banco Quilmes.

text.p: Argentina's Banco Quilmes SA said Monday that the Fiorito-Bianchi family had agreed to sell its controlling 70 percent stake to Canada's Bank of Nova Scotia, which already owns 25 percent of Quilmes.
Banco Quilmes made the announcement in a letter to the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange, in which there was no mention of how much the deal was worth.

A Banco Quilmes official told Reuters that the remaining five percent of Quilmes' share capital was in the hands of small investors "who will tender their shares as well, so Nova Scotia will have 100 percent of the share capital of Quilmes."

But he said no financial details could be released because the full announcement of the deal would not be made until this Wednesday, when details will be announced simultaneously in Canada and Argentina.
The Fiorito-Bianchi family has controlled Banco Quilmes since the mid-1960s and Nova Scotia came in with the purchase of a 25 percent stake two years ago.
Since then the bank has been on a "growth strategy" which will continue, the official said.

Banco Quilmes currently has 86 branches in Argentina. According to the Argentine banking association ADEBA, Banco Quilmes is ranked 13th in the country measured by deposits and 15th measured by loans.
